newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela CANTV sees improving margins in '97.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela CANTV sees improving margins in '97.

text.p: Venezuelan telephone company CANTV expects more improvement in profit margins this year on rising productivity and increased lines, company directors said in a conference call with investors.
"We plan to further reduce personnel, increasing the number of lines per employee. We expect good results for 1997," company President Gustavo Roosen said.
Currently threatened by labor action over wage offers for 1997 and 1998, Roosen said, "Union negotiations are proceeding as planned, albeit under difficult circumstances."
CANTV reported Wednesday better-than-expected year earnings of 208 billion bolivars for 1996 on a two percent fall in revenues to 693 billion bolivars, but a 19 percent fall in costs.
"That's some $436 million compared to last year's profits of $67 million," said executive vice president of finances Andres Glusky.
Roosen said 1997 would see important customer growth in its cellular telephone service, Movilnet, which rose 26 percent in 1996 to 214,000 users.
Backlogged Venezuelan demand for telephone lines totals around 500,000, he added. Last year, installed lines grew five percent, or 108,000 to reach 2.5 million.
